title: Crane Stability and Tip-Over Prevention
summary: A crane tips when the load exceeds capacity, goes outside the load chart, or the machine is not set up level on firm ground. This talk covers load weight, outriggers, and ground conditions.
talking_points: Know or calculate the weight of every load before you lift it.
Use the manufacturer's load chart for that crane and stay inside the safe operating range. Watch the load sensors on newer cranes.
Follow the manufacturer's outrigger procedure. Support outrigger pads on firm, stable ground and level the crane. Use crane mats or pads when needed.
Check the manufacturer's maximum wind speed and confirm it is safe to lift.
Check hoist brakes when making repeated heavy lifts from one spot.
Warn others of moving and overhead loads. Never carry a load over people or let people pass underneath. Never use visible tipping as a gauge of capacity.
site_hazards_to_check: Load weight unknown or not checked against the load chart
Outriggers not fully extended or pads on soft, sloped, or backfilled ground
Crane not level or not set up per the manufacturer's procedure
Wind at or above the crane's maximum rated speed
Workers walking or working under the load path
discussion_questions: What does this lift weigh, and where does it fall on the load chart?
Is the ground under the outriggers firm enough, and do we need mats?
Why is watching for the crane to start tipping a dangerous way to judge capacity?
